A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FoMo-0D research despite the changed title and formatting. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original FoMo-0D evaluations on ADBench and OpenOOD, runtime measurements, ablations, and attention and generalization analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds synthetic distribution-shift experiments and further analyses.

M1.justification: The GMM-based synthesis, PFN objective, router attention, linear-transform dataset reuse, and frozen contextual inference remain unchanged. Quantile preprocessing and the additional 100-epoch training experiment already appear in v2.

E1.justification: V3 Appendix G.1 adds synthetic test scenarios involving shifted means/covariances, more clusters, higher dimensionality, binary outliers, and combined shifts. These extend conditions within the existing OD task; the 57 ADBench datasets and ten OpenOOD tasks are retained.

E2.justification: The ADBench comparisons retain 26 baselines and four hyperparameter-averaged variants. OpenOOD retains DTE-NP, kNN, ICL, and DTE-C. The new synthetic tests evaluate FoMo-0D alone, and the performance profiles use existing comparators.

E3.justification: New synthetic tests use 1,000 test points, 5% outliers, and 5,000 context points. V3 also adds a quantile-transform control to the GMM-fit analysis and CDF-area performance aggregation. Section 3.1 corrects covariance bounds from [-5,5] to (0,5], but older bounds remain elsewhere; this does not establish rerunning the original experiments.

E4.justification: V3 substantially extends supplementary analysis with controlled synthetic distribution shifts in G.1, a with/without-quantile-transform GMM-fit comparison in Figure 16, and performance-profile analyses across metrics and dimensionality subsets in Appendix H. Existing ablations and the attention case study are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix G.1 newly specifies dataset-generation seeds 0–999 and reports means and standard deviations across 1,000 synthetic datasets per setting. This is additional seed and aggregation information, not an increase in runs for the retained benchmarks, whose five-seed reporting and Wilcoxon tests remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing detailed ADBench and OpenOOD scores are unchanged, but v3 adds substantial generalization findings and alternative aggregate rankings. Table 8 reports AUROC of 98.55±2.73 in-distribution versus 85.44±16.96 under combined shifts, and near-perfect binary-outlier detection. Appendix H adds CDF-area rankings, including first place on F1 across all datasets; these are new analyses, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(14), the formal definitions, and the Mahalanobis-distance and percentile-preservation proofs are retained. V2 Appendix C becomes v3 Appendix B with numbering and typesetting changes, without new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The central claims remain a first foundation model for zero-shot tabular OD, elimination of per-dataset training and model selection, competitive benchmark performance, and 7.7 ms average inference. The new research-directions bullet foregrounds questions already discussed in v2 rather than introducing a different core contribution.

C2.justification: V3 interprets sensitivity to shifted GMM parameters, possible generalization to discrete inputs, and degradation under combined shifts. It also removes v2's suggestion that p-values above 0.5 mean the odds favor FoMo-0D and more carefully distinguishes nonsignificance from equality. Most previously stated limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix G.1 documents generation ranges and binary-outlier construction for the new synthetic tests. Existing architecture, optimizer, hardware, preprocessing, and code/checkpoint access information are retained; their relocation does not establish implementation changes.

R1.justification: V3 adds Dolan and Moré (2002) for performance profiles and Zhou et al. (2024), AnomalyCLIP, for zero-shot anomaly detection. The existing related-work discussion largely moves from Appendix L into Section 5, with the research positioning retained.

P1.justification: V3 changes the title, edits the abstract and introduction, adds a research-directions bullet, moves related work into the main text, and reorders some appendices. Most methodological and experimental prose and the overall argument remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 substantially reformats typography, author information, text width, and figure placement. Figure 2 is enlarged, Tables 1–2 reorder rows, Figure 16 becomes a two-panel display with additional visual encodings, and a synthetic-results table and six performance-profile figures are added.

improvement.justification: The synthetic stress tests and added quantile-transform control make generalization evidence more informative, especially by documenting degradation under combined shifts. Performance profiles and more careful statistical wording improve interpretation. These are useful incremental gains over v2's already extensive evaluation; the core benchmark evidence is unchanged, and the covariance-range correction remains inconsistent elsewhere.
